**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 51, verses 56–60:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿I did not create the jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me﴾. It has been said: this is specific to those whom God foreknew would worship Him. It is phrased in general terms, but its meaning is particular. The meaning is: I did not create the people of felicity among the jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me in monotheism (tawhid). Al-Qushayri said: the verse has definitely been restricted, because the insane and the children were not commanded to worship, so it cannot be said that He intended worship from them. God Exalted has said: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind﴾ [see vol. 7, p. 324]. Whoever was created for Hell is not among those created for worship. Therefore the verse is to be understood as referring to the believers among them. This is like His saying: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed"﴾ [see vol. 16, p. 348]; what is meant is only that a group of them said so. This was mentioned by al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi, al-Farra' and al-Qutabi.

In the recitation (qira'ah) of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), it reads: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind from among the believers except that they should worship Me﴾. Ali (may God be pleased with him) said: that is, "I did not create the jinn and humankind except that I command them to worship." Al-Zajjaj relied on this view, and the saying of God Exalted supports it: ﴿And they were not commanded except that they should worship God, sincere to Him in religion, as monotheists﴾ [see vol. 8, p. 119]. If it is asked: how did they disbelieve when He created them to acknowledge His lordship and to submit to His command and will? It is answered: they submit to His decree over them, because His decree applies to them and they cannot resist it; the one who disbelieved only opposed them in acting upon what He commanded. As for submission to His decree, it is not something they can refuse.

It has also been said: ﴿except that they should worship Me﴾ means, except that they should acknowledge Me in worship, willingly or unwillingly. This was narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas. "Unwillingly" (al-karh) refers to what is seen in them of the traces of creation. Mujahid said: except that they should know Me.

Al-Tha'labi said: this is a good view, because if He had not created them, His existence and His oneness would not have been known. The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of God Exalted: ﴿If you ask them who created them, they will surely say, "God"﴾ and ﴿If you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, "The Mighty, the Knowing created them"﴾ [see vol. 16, p. 123 and p. 64], and what resembles these verses.

It is also narrated from Mujahid: except that I command them and forbid them. Zayd ibn Aslam said: it refers to what they were formed upon of wretchedness and felicity. So He created the fortunate among the jinn and humankind for worship, and He created the wretched among them for disobedience. It is also narrated from al-Kalbi: except that they should be monotheists. As for the believer, he affirms His oneness in hardship and ease; as for the disbeliever, he affirms His oneness in hardship and calamity but not in blessing and ease. The evidence for this is the saying of God Exalted: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [see vol. 14, p. 80], to the end of the verse.

Ikrimah said: ﴿except that they should worship and obey Me﴾, so I reward the worshipper and punish the one who denies.

It has been said: the meaning is "except that I may enslave them" (li-astu'bidahum). The meanings are close. It is said: "ʿabd bayyin al-ʿubūdah wa al-ʿubūdiyyah" (a servant clearly in servitude). The root of ʿubūdiyyah is submission and humiliation. Taʿbīd means to make something humble; one says: "a path made smooth (maʿbad)." Tarafah ibn al-Abd said, and the line is from his Mu'allaqah, its first half being:

*"They vie with swift, fleet-footed she-camels, and there followed—"*

(The wazīf is the lower part of the leg. His saying "wazīfan wazīfan" means that she set the hoof of her foot upon the hoof-print of her hand, which is praised in a camel when she walks. The mawr is the road.)

*"A wazīf after a wazīf, above a smoothed road."*

Taʿbīd is istiʿbād, which is to take someone as a slave; likewise iʿtibād. ʿIbādah is obedience, and taʿabbud is asceticism. So the meaning of ﴿to worship Me﴾ is: that they should be humbled, submit, and worship.

﴿I do not want any provision from them﴾. The word "min" (from) is extra, meaning: "any provision." Rather, I am the Provider and the Giver. Ibn Abbas and Abu al-Jawza' said: that is, I do not want them to provide for themselves, nor to feed themselves. It has also been said: the meaning is that I do not want them to provide for My servants, nor to feed them. ﴿Indeed God is the Provider﴾ [al-Razzaq]. Ibn Muhaysin and others read "al-Raziq" (the Provider, in the active form).

﴿The Possessor of strength, the Firm﴾: that is, the Mighty and the Strong. Al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Wathhab and al-Nakha'i read "al-Matin" in the genitive (jarr), as an adjective to "quwwah" (strength). The rest read it in the nominative (raf'), as an adjective to "al-Razzaq," or to "dhu" in His saying "dhu al-quwwah," or it may be the predicate of an omitted subject, or an adjective to the noun of "inna" according to its position, or a predicate after a predicate. Al-Farra' said: its correct form should have been "al-matinah" (feminine), but it was masculinized because it is taken to refer to a thing that is firm and well-twisted, as in "ḥablun matīn" (a strong rope). Al-Farra' recited:

*"For every age I have worn garments, until the head was covered by a white veil,*
*Of striped cloth and of yemeni cloth, the banded one."*

Here he said "al-muʿaṣṣab" (the banded one), because al-yumnah is a type of garment. From this same category is His saying: ﴿So whoever has received an admonition﴾ [see vol. 3, p. 359], meaning an exhortation (waʿẓ). And ﴿The cry seized those who did wrong﴾ [see vol. 9, p. 61], meaning the cries and the sound.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, for those who did wrong﴾, that is, those who disbelieved among the people of Makkah, ﴿a portion like the portion of their companions﴾, that is, a share of the punishment like the share of the disbelievers among the earlier nations. Ibn al-A'rabi said: it is said "a day of dhanūb," meaning a day of long evil that does not end. The original meaning of dhanūb in the language is a large bucket. They used to draw water and divide it into shares, so the share was called a dhanūb. The rajiz (poet) said:

*"For us is a dhanūb, and for you is a dhanūb;*
*If you refuse, then for us is the well."*

ʿAlqamah said:

*"Every day you have dealt out a favour,*
*So Shaʾs has a right to your generosity, a dhanūb."*

Another said (its speaker being Abu Dhu'ayb):

*"By your life, while the fates come upon us in succession,*
*For every family of a father there is a dhanūb from them."*

Al-Jawhari said: dhanūb is a horse with a long tail; dhanūb also means a share; dhanūb is meat under the back. Ibn al-Sikkit said: it is water roughly the amount of a full bucket; it may be feminine or masculine; it is not called dhanūb when it is empty. Its plural in the smallest number is adhnibah, and in the abundant number, dhanā'ib, like qalūṣ and qalā'iṣ.

﴿So let them not ask Me to hasten﴾, that is, let them not hasten the descent of the punishment upon them. For they said: "O Muhammad, bring upon us what you promise us, if you are among the truthful" [see vol. 7, p. 237 and vol. 9, p. 27]. So there descended upon them on the day of Badr what fulfilled His promise and hastened His vengeance upon them. Then for them in the Hereafter is the everlasting punishment and the enduring disgrace, which has no end.

It is phrased in general terms, but its meaning is particular. The meaning is: I did not create the people of felicity among the jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me in monotheism (tawhid). Al-Qushayri said: the verse has definitely been restricted, because the insane and the children were not commanded to worship, so it cannot be said that He intended worship from them. God Exalted has said: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind﴾ [see vol. 7, p. 324]. Whoever was created for Hell is not among those created for worship. Therefore the verse is to be understood as referring to the believers among them. This is like His saying: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed"﴾ [see vol. 16, p. 348]; what is meant is only that a group of them said so. This was mentioned by al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi, al-Farra' and al-Qutabi.

In the recitation (qira'ah) of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), it reads: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind from among the believers except that they should worship Me﴾. Ali (may God be pleased with him) said: that is, "I did not create the jinn and humankind except that I command them to worship." Al-Zajjaj relied on this view, and the saying of God Exalted supports it: ﴿And they were not commanded except that they should worship God, sincere to Him in religion, as monotheists﴾ [see vol. 8, p. 119]. If it is asked: how did they disbelieve when He created them to acknowledge His lordship and to submit to His command and will? It is answered: they submit to His decree over them, because His decree applies to them and they cannot resist it; the one who disbelieved only opposed them in acting upon what He commanded. As for submission to His decree, it is not something they can refuse.

It has also been said: ﴿except that they should worship Me﴾ means, except that they should acknowledge Me in worship, willingly or unwillingly. This was narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas.
